transcript.text: Sofia, Eddie, your research proposal is on AI writing tools in universities. Sofia, why this topic?
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: Honestly, because everyone's talking about it but few have data. Our department has no clear policy yet, and students are confused about what's allowed.
transcript.speaker: SOFIA

transcript.text: Also, we noticed that many lecturers use these tools themselves, so the situation is more complicated than people think.
transcript.speaker: EDDIE

transcript.text: That's an interesting angle. Is it part of the study?
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: Partly. Some interview questions will ask about lecturers' own experience.
transcript.speaker: SOFIA

transcript.text: We'll use mixed methods, a survey for breadth and interviews for depth.
transcript.speaker: EDDIE

transcript.text: Sample size?
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: We aimed for three hundred survey responses, though I suspect we'll get fewer, maybe two hundred, because it's exam season.
transcript.speaker: EDDIE

transcript.text: Exam season is a risk. Many students ignore surveys at that time.
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: We'll offer a small prize draw, which usually helps.
transcript.speaker: EDDIE

transcript.text: And the interviews?
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: Ten lecturers and ten students. We'll record them with permission and transcribe the audio automatically.
transcript.speaker: SOFIA

transcript.text: Automatic transcription isn't perfect. Budget time to correct it.
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: Good point. We estimated a week but it's probably two.
transcript.speaker: EDDIE

transcript.text: We'll also do a pilot with five students first, to test whether the questions are clear.
transcript.speaker: SOFIA

transcript.text: Good. A pilot always saves time later.
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: Now, your main hypothesis. Remind me.
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: That students who use AI tools frequently don't necessarily get higher marks, but they do report less anxiety about deadlines.
transcript.speaker: SOFIA

transcript.text: It's not a completely new idea, but nobody has tested it properly in our university.
transcript.speaker: EDDIE

transcript.text: That is exactly the kind of gap a good proposal should fill.
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: Let's fix the timeline. When does the survey open?
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: Mid-October, and it stays open for three weeks.
transcript.speaker: EDDIE

transcript.text: Then interviews in November, mostly on Wednesdays, when lecturers have fewer classes.
transcript.speaker: SOFIA

transcript.text: And the analysis?
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: We'll use the university's statistics software, which is free for students, and we'll finish by the end of January.
transcript.speaker: EDDIE

transcript.text: Reasonable. Make sure you keep a backup of all the data, in at least two places.
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: We'll use the university cloud and an external drive.
transcript.speaker: SOFIA

transcript.text: Ethics approval is essential. Who will you submit the application to?
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: The faculty ethics committee, I assume.
transcript.speaker: SOFIA

transcript.text: Not the faculty committee. For research involving staff, it must go to the central ethics board.
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: How long does that take?
transcript.speaker: EDDIE

transcript.text: Normally about a month, so apply this week.
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: And if we want to quote lecturers by name?
transcript.speaker: SOFIA

transcript.text: Don't. Anonymise everyone. Use codes instead.
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: That will also make it easier to protect the participants' privacy.
transcript.speaker: SOFIA

transcript.text: Exactly, and it will make your ethics application much smoother.
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: Understood, thank you.
transcript.speaker: EDDIE

transcript.text: Send me the revised proposal by the end of next week and we'll go through it together.
transcript.speaker: PROF LAWSON

transcript.text: Thank you, Professor. We'll get started straight away.
transcript.speaker: SOFIA
